headline: Net income drops on CECL charge, AFFO keeps growing
summary_short: VICI reported Q2 2026 revenue of $1,058.5M (+5.7% y/y), but net income attributable to common stockholders fell 39.1% y/y to $526.5M ($0.48/diluted share) on a $413.1M CECL allowance swing. AFFO nonetheless rose 7.8% y/y to $679.6M ($0.62/share).
summary_long: Revenue rose 5.7% y/y to $1,058.5M on contractual rent escalations plus three newly closed tenants: Clairvest's Northfield Park lease, the $1.16B Golden Entertainment Nevada portfolio, and the Gamehost casinos in Alberta. Net income fell 39.1% y/y to $526.5M ($0.48/diluted share) entirely on a $413.1M year-over-year swing in the non-cash CECL credit-loss allowance — a GAAP-only hit, not an operating decline. AFFO, which excludes that swing, rose 7.8% y/y to $679.6M ($0.62/share). VICI raised the low end of full-year 2026 AFFO guidance to $2,675-2,695M ($2.45-2.47/share) from $2,665-2,695M ($2.44-2.47/share); the high end is unchanged. Cash fell to $288.1M funding the Golden Entertainment and Gamehost deals; debt rose to $17.2B; dividend held at $0.45/share.

drivers.explanation: GAAP net income fell y/y almost entirely on a non-cash CECL allowance swing tied to tenant credit assumptions, while the company's own non-GAAP measure (AFFO) and quarterly revenue both grew; three new tenants closed in the quarter.

Contractual escalations across existing master leases plus new/incremental rent from the Golden Entertainment Master Lease ($14.5M), Clairvest Northfield Park Lease ($10.5M), and PURE Master Lease Gamehost addition drove the y/y increase.
The y/y decrease was driven, on an absolute basis, by a $413.1M aggregate change in the CECL allowance for credit losses between the two quarters — the release states this explicitly as the cause.

This Yahoo-derived figure equals total revenue less golf-course operating expenses only; VICI as a triple-net-lease REIT discloses no distinct cost-of-revenue line, so the move simply tracks the revenue increase.

Total expenses swung from a $93.1M net benefit (Q2 2025, when the CECL allowance released $142.0M) to a $315.6M expense (Q2 2026, when the allowance charged $271.1M), which is the full explanation for the operating-income decline against a revenue increase.
Tracks the same CECL-allowance-driven operating-income decline described above; EBIT and operating income are nearly identical this quarter.
EBITDA exceeds EBIT by only the $1.0M of quarterly depreciation the release discloses, so it moves in lockstep with the CECL-driven operating-income decline.
Tracks the CECL-allowance-driven operating decline; interest expense was roughly flat y/y ($209.9M vs $213.8M).

EPS fell in line with the CECL-driven net-income decline, compounded slightly by a 3.1% y/y rise in diluted share count from the Golden Entertainment stock-for-stock exchange and forward-sale settlement.

This line is golf-course operating expenses only (the release's own AFFO-reconciliation definition); it is not a company-wide cost-of-revenue figure and its small y/y rise is not discussed in the release.

Cash fell q/q as VICI funded the $1.16B Golden Entertainment acquisition (assumed and retired $426.0M of Golden Entertainment debt) and the C$200.6M Gamehost Portfolio acquisition using cash on hand plus a revolver draw.
Debt rose modestly q/q on a C$185.0M revolving-credit draw to help fund the Gamehost acquisition, partially offset by the retirement of Golden Entertainment's assumed $426.0M of debt.
Equity grew on the approximately 24.3 million VICI shares issued to former Golden Entertainment shareholders in the stock-for-stock exchange, plus retained-earnings accretion from net income.
Share count rose on the Golden Entertainment share issuance (24.3M shares) and the physical settlement of the remaining 7,750,000 shares under VICI's outstanding forward sale agreement.
